images.alt: Diagram shows the Account dimension table relating to the Transaction fact table, and the Customer dimension table relating via the Customer Account bridge table, because customers can have multiple accounts and accounts can have multiple customers.
images.credit: Microsoft Learn — Modeling Dimension Tables in Warehouse, Microsoft Fabric documentation

imageNote: Genuine Microsoft-authored diagram exists for this exact concept — the Fabric dimensional-modeling-dimension-tables page's 'Multivalued dimensions' section shows the real bank-account/customer bridge-table pattern (Account dimension, Transaction fact, Customer dimension linked via a Customer Account bridge table). Downloaded and used as the lesson's single screenshot slide. The Power BI many-to-many guidance page independently confirms the identical technique (its own bank-account-customer-model example), used as supporting research only, not a second image, to avoid redundancy.
